VERSUS  V SRINIVASAN & ORS. 
 (IA No. 135433/2019 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL  DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES and IA No. 133329/2019 - PERMISSION TO  FILE ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES)
 Date : 08-04-2025 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PANKAJ MITHAL  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.V.N. BHATTI

For Petitioner(s) Mr. Siddhartha Dave, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. G. Balaji, AOR  Mr. Neeleshwar Pavani, Adv.
 Ms. Arzu Paul, Adv.
 Mr. Yuvaraj Singh Rathore, Adv.
 Mr. Himanshu Tyagi, Adv.
 Ms. Alekhya Shastry, Adv.
 For Respondent(s) Mr. A. Karthik, AOR  Ms. Smrithi Suresh, Adv.
 Mr. Ujjwal Sharma, Adv.
 Mr. Sugam Agrawal, Adv.
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. ... vs V Srinivasan on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180450307/
1
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. On account of the road accident, on a claim Reason: preferred before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal1, the compensation of Rs.40,40,000/- 1 hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal.
(Rupees forty lakhs forty thousand)

was awarded holding that both the drivers are equally responsible and accordingly, the liability was apportioned in the ratio of 50:50 between the two insurers.
3.
The aforesaid amount awarded carried an interest of 7.5%.

4. The High Court allowed the appeal and exonerated the New India Assurance Company Ltd.-
Respondent No.3 from the liability.
5. It is against the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court that the other Insurer has preferred this special leave petition.

6. One of the contentions raised before us is that the claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was not maintainable and the appropriate remedy available to the petitioner was to file a claim under the Workmens Compensation Act, 1923.

7. In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, looking to the fact that one leg of the claimant has been amputated and he is completely bedridden, on account of his injury sustained, we consider it proper to give quietus to the matter.
8. Accordingly, as a special case, we allow the claimants compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-(Rupees twenty-five lakhs).
The petitioner has already deposited a sum of Rs.20,20,000/-(Rupees twenty lakhs twenty thousand) out of which Rs.12,00,000/- (Rupees twelve lakhs) has been withdrawn by the claimant.

9. The balance amount would be deposited by the petitioner within a month with interest of 6%
before the Tribunal.
10. The claimant is entitled to withdraw the said amount.
11. The present petition is disposed of in the above terms.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(SNEHA DAS) (NIDHI MATHUR)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT COURT MASTER (NSH)
